## Appendix I Proof of Theorem 7

The key is to analyze the random-design setting and show that its minimax rate of Hamming error is only determined by $\mathbb{E}[X^{\prime}X]=\Sigma$ . Then, when we switch to the fixed-design case of $X^{\prime}X=\Sigma$ , the same minimax rate holds. For the random-design setting, we proceed by deriving a lower bound and an upper bound of the minimax Hamming error separately.

First, we derive a lower bound for the minimax Hamming error. Let $G=X^{\prime}X$ denote the Gram matrix of the random-design model. Fixing any two subsets $V_{0},V_{1}\subset\{1,2,\ldots,p\}$ , we write $V=V_{0}\cup V_{1}$ . Let $\eta\in\{0,1\}^{p}$ be an arbitrary binary vector. We consider two binary vectors $\mu^{(0)},\mu^{(1)}\in\{0,1\}^{p}$ where $\mu^{(0)}_{j}=\mu^{(1)}_{j}=\eta_{j}$ , for $j\notin V$ , and restricted on $V$ , $\mathrm{Supp}(\mu^{(0)}_{V})=V_{0}$ and $\mathrm{Supp}(\mu_{V}^{(1)})=V_{1}$ . Let $\tau_{p}=\sqrt{2r\log(p)}$ . Consider the testing problem

$$ H_{0}:\beta=\tau_{p}\mu^{(0)},\qquad v.s.\qquad H_{1}:\beta=\tau_{p}\mu^{(1)}. $$

For a test $T$ , let $R(T)$ be the sum of type I and type II errors. Any selector $\hat{\beta}$ can be converted to a test $T(\hat{\beta})$ , where we reject the null hypothesis if $\mathrm{Supp}(\hat{\beta})\neq V_{0}$ . It is seen that $R(T(\hat{\beta}))=\mathbb{P}\{\beta=\tau_{p}\mu^{(0)},\mathrm{Supp}(\hat{\beta})\neq V_{0}\}+\mathbb{P}\{\beta=\tau_{p}\mu^{(1)},\mathrm{Supp}(\hat{\beta})=V_{0})\}\leq\sum_{j\in V}\{\mathbb{P}(\beta_{j}=0,\hat{\beta}_{j}\neq\tau_{p})+\mathbb{P}(\beta_{j}=\tau_{p},\hat{\beta}_{j}=0)\}$ . It follows that

$$ \mathbb{E}[H(\hat{\beta}_{V},\beta_{V})|X]\geq R(T(\hat{\beta}))\geq\inf_{T}R(T)\equiv R^{*}(V_{0},V_{1};\eta,X). $$

We can compute the right hand side using the Neyman-Pearson lemma. Define

$$ a=a(V_{0},V_{1},X)=(\mu^{(0)}-\mu^{(1)})^{\prime}G(\mu^{(0)}-\mu^{(1)}). $$

The likelihood ratio test for (93) is equivalent to using the test statistic $Z=a^{-1/2}(\mu^{(1)}-\mu^{(0)})^{\prime}X^{\prime}(y-\tau_{p}X\mu^{(0)})$ . Then, $Z\sim{\cal N}(0,1)$ under $H_{0}$ , and $Z\sim{\cal N}(a^{1/2}\tau_{p},1)={\cal N}(\sqrt{2ar\log(p)},1)$ , under $H_{1}$ . By Neyman-Pearson lemma,

$$ \displaystyle R^{*}(V_{0},V_{1};\eta,X) \displaystyle=\inf_{t}\Bigl\{\epsilon_{p}^{|V_{0}|}\cdot\mathbb{P}\bigl({\cal N}(0,1)>t\bigr)+\epsilon_{p}^{|V_{1}|}\cdot\mathbb{P}\bigl({\cal N}(\sqrt{2ar\log(p)},1)<t\bigr)\Bigr\} \displaystyle=\inf_{t=\sqrt{2q\log(p)}}\Bigl\{L_{p}p^{-|V_{0}|\vartheta-q}+L_{p}p^{-|V_{1}|\vartheta-(\sqrt{ar}-\sqrt{q})_{+}^{2}}\Bigr\} \displaystyle=L_{p}p^{-h(V_{0},V_{1},X)}, $$

where

$$ h(V_{0},V_{1},X)=\max_{q>0}\Bigl(\min\Bigl\{|V_{0}|\vartheta+q,\;|V_{1}|\vartheta+(\sqrt{ar}-\sqrt{q})_{+}^{2}\Bigr\}\Bigr). $$

In the second line of (96), we have used the Mills’ ratio of $N(0,1)$ (e.g., see Ke et al. (2014) for a similar use of the Mills’ ratio). Let $\Sigma$ be the covariance matrix, parameterized by $\rho$ . We define the following quantities:

$$ \displaystyle a^{*}(V_{0},V_{1},\rho) \displaystyle=(\mu^{(0)}-\mu^{(1)})^{\prime}\Sigma(\mu^{(0)}-\mu^{(1)}), \displaystyle h^{*}(V_{0},V_{1},\rho) \displaystyle=\max_{q>0}\Bigl(\min\Bigl\{|V_{0}|\vartheta+q,\;|V_{1}|\vartheta+(\sqrt{a^{*}r}-\sqrt{q})_{+}^{2}\Bigr\}\Bigr). $$

Below, we show that $h(V_{0},V_{1},X)$ is sufficiently close to $h^{*}(V_{0},V_{1},\rho)$ . The key is showing that $\Sigma$ and $G$ are sufficiently close on the diagonal block restricted to $V$ . We use Theorem 5.39 and Remark 5.40 of Vershynin (2012) with $t=O(\sqrt{|V|\log(p)})$ . It follows that, when $|V|\ll n$ , with probability $1-o(p^{-3-|V|})$ ,

$$ \|G_{V,V}-\Sigma_{V,V}\|\leq C\|\Sigma_{V,V}\|\sqrt{n^{-1}|V|\log(p)};\quad\mbox{here, $C$ a constant independent of $|V|$}. $$

We note that $\|\Sigma_{V,V}\|\leq\|\Sigma\|\leq C$ . For any finite integer $m\geq 1$ , the total number of size- $m$ subset $V$ is ${p\choose m}=O(p^{m})$ . We then apply the probability union bound to get that, with probability $1-O(p^{-3})$ ,

$$ \max_{V:|V|\leq m}\|G_{V,V}-\Sigma_{V,V}\|\leq C\sqrt{n^{-1}\log(p)}. $$

Since $|a(V_{0},V_{1},X)-a^{*}(V_{0},V_{1},\rho)|\leq\|G_{V,V}-\Sigma_{V,V}\|\cdot\|\mu^{(1)}-\mu^{(0)}\|^{2}\leq\|G_{V,V}-\Sigma_{V,V}\|\cdot|V|$ , we immediately know that

$$ |a(V_{0},V_{1},X)-a^{*}(V_{0},V_{1},\rho)|\leq C\sqrt{n^{-1}\log(p)}\quad\mbox{here, $C$ depends on $m$}. $$

Write $h=h(V_{0},V_{1},X)$ and $h^{*}=h^{*}(V_{0},V_{1},\rho)$ for short, and let $(h^{*},a^{*})$ be the shorthand notations defined similarly. Then, $h=\max_{q}g(q,a)$ and $h^{*}=\max_{q}f(q,a^{*})$ , for $f(q,a)=\min\{|V_{0}|\vartheta+q,|V_{1}|\vartheta+(\sqrt{ar}-\sqrt{q})_{+}^{2}\}$ . Let $\tilde{q}$ and $\tilde{q}^{*}$ be the two maximizers. It is seen that $h=f(\tilde{q},a)\leq f(\tilde{q},a^{*})+\max_{q}|f(q,a)-f(q,a^{*})|\leq h^{*}+\max_{q}|f(q,a)-f(q,a^{*})|$ . Similarly, we can also derive that $h\leq h^{*}+\max_{q}|f(q,a^{*})-f(q,a)|$ . Combining them gives $|h-h^{*}|\leq\max_{q}|f(q,a^{*})-f(q,a)|$ . We plug in the expression of $f(q,a)$ to get

$$ |h(V_{0},V_{1},X)-h^{*}(V_{0},V_{1},\rho)|\leq|\sqrt{ar}-\sqrt{a^{*}r}|\leq C\sqrt{n^{-1}\log(p)}. $$

We now combine all the results, and note that (101) has a maximum over all $V=V_{0}\cup V_{1}$ . It follows that, with probability $1-O(p^{-3})$ ,

$$ \max_{(V_{0},V_{1}):|V_{0}\cup V_{1}|\leq m}|h(V_{0},V_{1},X)-h^{*}(V_{0},V_{1},\rho)|\leq C\sqrt{n^{-1}\log(p)}. $$

We plug it into (96). Note that $L_{p}p^{-h}=L_{p}p^{-h^{*}}\cdot p^{h^{*}-h}$ . In line of (103), $p^{h^{*}-h}$ is a multi- $\log(p)$ term, i.e., $L_{p}p^{-h}=L_{p}p^{-h^{*}}$ . We then combine it with (94). It yields that, with probability $1-O(p^{-3})$ ,

$$ \mathbb{E}[H(\hat{\beta}_{V},\beta_{V})|X]\geq L_{p}p^{-h^{*}(V_{0},V_{1},\rho)},\mbox{simultaneously for all $(V_{0},V_{1})$ with $|V_{0}\cup V_{1}|\leq m$}. $$

Given $V$ , we further take a maximum over $(V_{0},V_{1})$ on the right hand side. It follows that

$$ \mathbb{E}[H(\hat{\beta}_{V},\beta_{V})|X]\geq L_{p}p^{-h^{**}(V,\rho)},\qquad\mbox{where}\quad h^{**}(V,\rho)=\min_{\begin{subarray}{c}(V_{0},V_{1}):V_{0}\neq V_{1},\\
V_{0}\cup V_{1}=V\end{subarray}}h^{*}(V_{0},V_{1},\rho). $$

Write $\{1,2,\ldots,p\}=\cup_{j=1}^{\lceil p/2\rceil}V_{j}$ , where $V_{j}=\{2j-1,2j\}$ for $j\leq p/2$ and $V_{j}=\{p\}$ for $j>p/2$ (this happens only if $p$ is odd). It follows that, with probability $1-O(p^{-3})$ ,

$$ \mathbb{E}[H(\hat{\beta},\beta)|X]=\sum_{1\leq j\leq\lceil p/2\rceil}\mathbb{E}[H(\hat{\beta}_{V_{j}},\beta_{V_{j}})|X]\geq\sum_{1\leq j\leq\lceil p/2\rceil}L_{p}p^{-h^{**}(V_{j},\rho)}. $$

When $p$ is even, $h^{**}(V_{j},\rho)$ are all equal. When $p$ is odd, $h^{**}(V_{j},\rho)$ are all equal, except for one $V_{j}$ ; but this one has a negligible effect on the right hand side above. Let $h^{**}(\rho)$ be the common value of $h^{**}(V_{j},\rho)$ . Since $h^{**}(\rho)$ also depends on $(\vartheta,r)$ , we write it as $h^{**}(\rho;\vartheta,r)$ to reflect this dependence. We immediately have that, with probability $1-O(p^{-3})$ ,

$$ \mathbb{E}[H(\hat{\beta},\beta)|X]\geq L_{p}p^{1-h^{**}(\rho;\vartheta,r)}. $$

On the event that the above inequality does not hold, the Hamming error is at most $p$ . The contribution of this event to the expected Hamming error is at most $p\cdot O(p^{-3})=O(p^{-2})$ , which is negligible to $L_{p}p^{1-h^{*}(\rho;\vartheta,r)}$ . It follows that

$$ \mathbb{E}[H(\hat{\beta},\beta)]\geq L_{p}p^{1-h^{**}(\rho;\vartheta,r)},\qquad\mbox{for any method $\hat{\beta}$}. $$

This gives a lower bound for the minimax Hamming error.

Next, we give an upper bound for the minimax Hamming error. We will consider a specific $\hat{\beta}$ . Let the partition $\{1,2,\ldots,p\}=\cup_{j=1}^{\lceil p/2\rceil}V_{j}$ be the same as above. For any subset $U\subset\{1,2,\ldots,p\}$ , let ${\bf 1}_{U}$ be the binary vector such that its $j$ th entry is $1$ if $j\in U$ and $0$ otherwise. Additionally, let $X_{U}$ be the submatrix of $X$ restricted to columns in $U$ . For each $V_{j}$ , define

$$ \hat{U}_{j}=\argmin_{U\subset V_{j}}\Bigl\{\frac{1}{2}\|y-\tau_{p}X{\bf 1}_{U}\|^{2}+\vartheta\log(p)|U|\Bigr\}. $$

Define $\hat{\mu}\in\{0,1\}^{p}$ such that for any $i\in V_{j}$ , $\hat{\mu}_{i}=1$ if $i\in\hat{U}_{j}$ , and $\hat{\mu}_{i}=0$ otherwise. The estimator is $\hat{\beta}=\tau_{p}\hat{\mu}$ . We now calculate the expected Hamming error of this estimator. Let $S$ be the support of $\beta$ . Fix $V_{j}$ and write $V=V_{j}$ for short. Given any two subsets $U_{0}$ and $U_{1}$ of $V$ such that $U_{0}\neq U_{1}$ , we consider the event

$$ \mathrm{Supp}(\beta_{V})=U_{0},\qquad\mathrm{Supp}(\hat{\beta}_{V})=U_{1},\qquad|S|\leq 2p^{1-\vartheta}. $$

On this event, it is true that

$$ \frac{1}{2}\|y-\tau_{p}X{\bf 1}_{U_{0}}\|^{2}+\vartheta\log(p)|U_{0}|\geq\frac{1}{2}\|y-\tau_{p}X{\bf 1}_{U_{1}}\|^{2}+\vartheta\log(p)|U_{1}|. $$

Note that $y=X\beta+z=\tau_{p}X{\bf 1}_{U_{0}}+\tau_{p}X{\bf 1}_{S\cap V^{c}}+z$ . We can re-write (109) as

$$ \frac{1}{2}\|z+\tau_{p}X{\bf 1}_{S\cap V^{c}}\|^{2}+\vartheta\log(p)|U_{0}|\geq\frac{1}{2}\|(z+\tau_{p}X{\bf 1}_{S\cap V^{c}})-\tau_{p}X({\bf 1}_{U_{1}}-{\bf 1}_{U_{0}})\|^{2}+\vartheta\log(p)|U_{1}|. $$

Let $F=U_{0}\cap U_{1}$ , $E_{0}=U_{0}\setminus F$ and $E_{1}=U_{1}\setminus F$ . Then, $|U_{0}|=|F|+|E_{0}|$ and $|U_{1}|=|F|+|E_{1}|$ . We plug it into the above inequality and re-arrange the terms. It gives

$$ z^{\prime}X({\bf 1}_{U_{1}}-{\bf 1}_{U_{0}})\geq\frac{\tau_{p}}{2}({\bf 1}_{U_{1}}-{\bf 1}_{U_{0}})^{\prime}G({\bf 1}_{U_{1}}-{\bf 1}_{U_{0}})-{\bf 1}_{S\cap V^{c}}^{\prime}G({\bf 1}_{U_{1}}-{\bf 1}_{U_{0}})+\frac{\vartheta\log(p)}{\tau_{p}}(|E_{1}|-|E_{0}|). $$

Let $a=a(U_{0},U_{1},X)=({\bf 1}_{U_{1}}-{\bf 1}_{U_{0}})^{\prime}G({\bf 1}_{U_{1}}-{\bf 1}_{U_{0}})$ . We note that this definition is indeed the same as that in (95). Let $\tilde{z}=z^{\prime}X({\bf 1}_{U_{1}}-{\bf 1}_{U_{0}})/\sqrt{a}$ . The above can be written equivalently as

$$ \tilde{z}\geq\sqrt{2\log(p)}\biggl[\frac{\sqrt{ra}}{2}-\frac{{\bf 1}_{S\cap V^{c}}^{\prime}G({\bf 1}_{U_{1}}-{\bf 1}_{U_{0}})}{\sqrt{a}}+\frac{\vartheta(|E_{1}|-|E_{0}|)}{2\sqrt{ra}}\biggr],\quad\mbox{where}\;\;\tilde{z}|(X,\beta)\sim N(0,1). $$

We bound $|{\bf 1}_{S\cap V^{c}}^{\prime}G({\bf 1}_{U_{1}}-{\bf 1}_{U_{0}})|$ . Since $\Sigma_{V^{c}V}$ is a zero matrix, we immediately have ${\bf 1}_{S\cap V^{c}}^{\prime}\Sigma({\bf 1}_{U_{1}}-{\bf 1}_{U_{0}})=0$ . It follows by the triangle inequality that

$$ \displaystyle|{\bf 1}_{S\cap V^{c}}^{\prime}G({\bf 1}_{U_{1}}-{\bf 1}_{U_{0}})| \displaystyle\leq|{\bf 1}_{S\cap V^{c}}^{\prime}(G-\Sigma)({\bf 1}_{U_{1}}-{\bf 1}_{U_{0}})| \displaystyle\leq|V|\cdot\max_{k\in V}|e_{k}^{\prime}(G-\Sigma){\bf 1}_{S\cap V^{c}}|. $$

For $k\in V$ , $e_{k}^{\prime}(G-\Sigma){\bf 1}_{S\cap V^{c}}=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{\ell\in S\cap V^{c}}\{X(i,k)X(i,\ell)-\mathbb{E}[X(i,k)X(i,\ell)]\}$ . We recall that $\{1,2,\ldots,p\}=\cup_{m=1}^{\lceil p/2\rceil}V_{m}$ is a partition. It induces a partition on $S\cap V^{c}$ , which we denote by $S\cap V^{c}=\cup_{m=1}^{N_{p}}S_{m}$ . Each $S_{m}$ contains at most 2 indices and $|S\cap V^{c}|/2\leq N_{p}\leq|S\cap V^{c}|$ . Write

$$ e_{k}^{\prime}(G-\Sigma){\bf 1}_{S\cap V^{c}}=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{m=1}^{N_{p}}\Bigl[\sum_{\ell\in S_{m}}\{X(i,k)X(i,\ell)-\mathbb{E}[X(i,k)X(i,\ell)]\}\Bigr]. $$

The right hand side is a sum of $nN_{p}$ independent variables, where each variable has a zero mean and a sub-exponential norm bounded by $n^{-1}K$ , for a constant $K>0$ . We apply the Bernstein inequality (Vershynin, 2012, Proposition 5.16) to get that, for every $t>0$ ,

$$ \mathbb{P}\bigl(|e_{k}^{\prime}(G-\Sigma){\bf 1}_{S\cap V^{c}}|>t\bigr)\leq 2\exp\Bigl(-c\min\Bigl\{\frac{nt^{2}}{K^{2}N_{p}},\frac{nt}{K}\Bigr\}\Bigr), $$

where $c>0$ is a universal constant. By letting $t=C\sqrt{n^{-1}N_{p}\log(p)}$ for a properly large constant $C$ , we have that, with probability $1-O(p^{-3})$ ,

$$ |e_{k}^{\prime}(G-\Sigma){\bf 1}_{S\cap V^{c}}|\leq C\sqrt{n^{-1}N_{p}\log(p)}\leq C\sqrt{n^{-1}|S|\log(p)}. $$

We plug it into (110) and apply the probability union bound. We also note that $|S|=O(p^{1-\vartheta})$ on the event (108); also, $n=p^{\omega}$ with $\omega>1-\vartheta$ . It follows that, on this event, with probability $1-O(p^{-3})$ ,

$$ |{\bf 1}_{S\cap V^{c}}^{\prime}G({\bf 1}_{U_{1}}-{\bf 1}_{U_{0}})|\leq Cp^{-(\omega-1+\vartheta)/2}\sqrt{\log(p)}. $$

We plug (113) into (110) to get:

$$ \tilde{z}\geq\sqrt{2b_{p}\log(p)},\quad\mbox{where }b_{p}=\Bigl[\frac{\sqrt{ra}}{2}+\frac{\vartheta(|E_{1}|-|E_{0}|)}{2\sqrt{ra}}-L_{p}p^{-\frac{\omega-1+\vartheta}{2}}\Bigr]^{2}. $$

Moreover, let $a^{*}=a^{*}(U_{0},U_{1},\rho)=({\bf 1}_{U_{1}}-{\bf 1}_{U_{0}})^{\prime}\Sigma({\bf 1}_{U_{1}}-{\bf 1}_{U_{0}})$ , which is the same as the definition in (99). By (102), the replacement of $a$ by $a^{*}$ only yields a difference of $L_{p}p^{-\frac{\omega-1+\vartheta}{2}}$ in the expression of $b_{p}$ . We further have:

$$ \tilde{z}\geq\sqrt{2b_{p}\log(p)},\quad\mbox{where }\tilde{z}|(X,\beta)\sim N(0,1)\mbox{ and }b_{p}=\Bigl[\frac{\sqrt{ra^{*}}}{2}+\frac{\vartheta(|E_{1}|-|E_{0}|)}{2\sqrt{ra^{*}}}+L_{p}p^{-\frac{\omega-1+\vartheta}{2}}\Bigr]^{2}. $$

First, what (114) says is that, conditioning on $(X,\beta_{V},\beta_{V^{c}})$ , if $\|\beta\|_{0}\leq Cp^{1-\vartheta}$ , then except for an event of probability $O(p^{-3})$ , $\mathrm{Supp}(\hat{\beta}_{V})=U_{1}$ implies $\tilde{z}>\sqrt{2b_{p}\log(p)}$ . Second, under our model, $(X,\beta_{V^{c}})$ are independent of $\beta_{V}$ , and $\mathbb{P}(\mathrm{Supp}(\beta_{V})=U_{0})=L_{p}p^{-\vartheta|U_{0}|}=L_{p}p^{-\vartheta(|F|+|E_{0}|)}$ . Last, $\mathbb{P}(\|\beta_{V^{c}}\|_{0}\leq 2p^{1-\vartheta})=1-O(p^{-3})$ (this is seen by noticing that $\|\beta_{V^{c}}\|_{0}$ is the sum of independent Bernoulli variables and by applying the Bernstein’s inequality). We combine the above to get

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{P}\bigl(\mathrm{Supp}(\beta_{V})=U_{0},\,\mathrm{Supp}(\hat{\beta}_{V})=U_{1},\,|S|\leq 2p^{1-\vartheta}\bigr) \displaystyle\leq\;\; \displaystyle L_{p}p^{-\vartheta|U_{0}|}\cdot\mathbb{P}\biggl(\tilde{z}\geq\sqrt{2b_{p}\log(p)}\biggr)+O(p^{-3}) \displaystyle\leq\;\; \displaystyle L_{p}p^{-\vartheta(|F|+|E_{0}|)-\bigl[\frac{\sqrt{ra^{*}}}{2}+\frac{\vartheta(|E_{1}|-|E_{0}|)}{2\sqrt{ra^{*}}}\bigr]_{+}^{2}}. $$

By elementary calculations, we have

$$ \displaystyle\vartheta(|F|+|E_{0}|)+\Bigl[\frac{\sqrt{ra^{*}}}{2}+\frac{\vartheta(|E_{1}|-|E_{0}|)}{2\sqrt{ra^{*}}}\Bigr]_{+}^{2} \displaystyle\geq\quad \displaystyle\vartheta|F|+\max\{|E_{0}|,|E_{1}|\}\vartheta+\frac{1}{4}\Bigl(\sqrt{ra^{*}}-\frac{|(|E_{1}|-|E_{0}|)|}{\sqrt{ra^{*}}}\Bigr)_{+}^{2} \displaystyle=\quad \displaystyle\max\{|U_{0}|,|U_{1}|\}\vartheta+\frac{1}{4}\Bigl(\sqrt{ra^{*}}-\frac{|(|U_{1}|-|U_{0}|)|}{\sqrt{ra^{*}}}\Bigr)_{+}^{2}\quad=\quad h^{*}(U_{0},U_{1},\rho), $$

where $h^{*}(U_{0},U_{1},\rho)$ is the same as that defined in (99) (the last equality above follows by solving $q$ in (99)). We combine the above to get

$$ \mathbb{P}\bigl(\mathrm{Supp}(\beta_{V})=U_{0},\,\mathrm{Supp}(\hat{\beta}_{V})=U_{1},\,|S|\leq 2p^{1-\vartheta}\bigr)\leq L_{p}p^{-h^{*}(U_{0},U_{1},\rho)}. $$

On the above event, the Hamming error contributed by $\hat{\beta}_{V}$ is $|E_{0}|+|E_{1}|\leq|V|\leq 2$ . Moreover, $h^{*}(U_{0},U_{1},\rho)\geq h^{**}(\rho;\vartheta,r)$ , where the latter is defined in (105). It follows that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[H(\hat{\beta}_{V},\beta_{V})] \displaystyle=\sum_{(U_{0},U_{1})}2\cdot\mathbb{P}\bigl(\mathrm{Supp}(\beta_{V})=U_{0},\,\mathrm{Supp}(\hat{\beta}_{V})=U_{1},\,|S|\leq 2p^{1-\vartheta}\bigr)+O(p^{-3}) \displaystyle\leq L_{p}\sum_{(U_{0},U_{1})}p^{-h^{*}(U_{0},U_{1},\rho)}\leq L_{p}p^{-h^{**}(\rho;\vartheta,r)}. $$

The above is true for every $V=V_{j}$ in the partition $\{1,2,\ldots,p\}=\cup_{j=1}^{\lceil p/2\rceil}$ (except for the last $V_{j}$ in the case that $p$ is odd; but this single $V_{j}$ has a negligible effect on the rate of the Hamming error). We immediately have

$$ \mathbb{E}[H(\hat{\beta},\beta)]=\sum_{1\leq j\leq\lceil p/2\rceil}\mathbb{E}[H(\hat{\beta}_{V},\beta_{V})]\leq L_{p}p^{1-h^{**}(\rho;\vartheta,r)},\quad\mbox{for the $\hat{\beta}$ in \eqref{proof-equivalent-8}}. $$

This gives an upper bound for the minimax Hamming error.

Last, we use (106) and (116) to show the claim. By combining these two inequalities, we know that, for the random design,

$$ \inf_{\hat{\beta}}\mathbb{E}[H(\hat{\beta},\beta)]=L_{p}p^{1-h^{**}(\rho;\vartheta,r)}. $$

A key observation is that the exponent $h^{**}(\rho;\vartheta,r)$ is only related to $\Sigma$ , not the realization of $X^{\prime}X$ . Now, we can mimic all the above derivations to get the same conclusion when the Gram matrix is fixed at $\Sigma$ (the proof is very similar, except that we now have $G=\Sigma$ ). Therefore, the minimax rates of the Hamming errors under two settings are exactly the same. ∎
